title: Project skills and plugins — decisions still open

steps.headline: What should an automatically enabled skill give your assistant at the start of a conversation?
steps.today: The assistant can see a list of installed skills and read a skill's full instructions when it uses that skill. You chose project-level controls for which skills are available automatically.
steps.problem: 'Enabled automatically' could mean knowing a skill exists or reading all of its instructions at the start. Those behave differently when many skills are installed.
steps.proposal: Choose what the assistant gets by default in a project. A skill used manually still stays in that conversation's history; this choice does not change that.

options.label: Know, then read
pros: The assistant knows when the skill might help without reading every full skill up front.
cons: It must take a separate step to read the skill when needed.

options.label: Read at start
pros: The skill's full instructions are available immediately.
cons: Every enabled skill adds its full text to the start of every conversation.

steps.headline: How should a new skill added outside the marketplace behave before you configure it?
steps.today: YouCoded discovers skills you put in your personal skill folder or a project's skill folder without a marketplace download. Existing items should keep working when these controls arrive.
steps.problem: A file added later could begin appearing automatically even though a freshly downloaded marketplace plugin begins inactive everywhere.
steps.proposal: Choose the default for newly discovered personal and project skill files. Existing files keep their current behavior either way.

options.label: Keep current behavior
pros: A skill you add yourself works the way it does today without another setup step.
cons: Marketplace downloads and hand-added skills have different defaults.

options.label: Require enabling
pros: All newly added skills wait for an explicit project choice.
cons: Adding a skill file alone would no longer make it automatically available.

steps.path: Projects → enable a plugin or one of its parts
steps.headline: Which automatic plugin behaviors should trigger the risk confirmation?
steps.today: You decided that enabling automatic parts should show one confirmation each time, listing all affected parts when a whole plugin is enabled.
steps.problem: A skill the assistant can choose to read, a server it connects to, and a hook that runs commands can carry different risks. Warning on everything may make real warnings easy to ignore.
steps.proposal: Pick the threshold for that confirmation. The dialog's exact wording and layout can wait for UI review.

options.label: Active behaviors
pros: Warns when enabling things that can connect or run by themselves, such as servers and hooks.
cons: Automatically discoverable skills would not get this warning.

options.label: Every automatic item
pros: One consistent confirmation rule for everything made automatic.
cons: Frequent warnings for ordinary skills may dilute the more serious ones.

options.label: Based on risk
pros: The warning can focus on actions that deserve attention.
cons: We would need to agree on a clear rule for which items count as risky before building it.

steps.path: Projects → plugin controls on another device
steps.headline: What should happen to a personally added skill when its project's choices reach a device without that file?
steps.today: You decided project choices should sync but plugins should not install automatically. Marketplace plugins missing on another device will show an Install action; credentials and device-specific settings will not sync.
steps.problem: A hand-added skill might not have a marketplace copy to install, even though the project remembers its setting.
steps.proposal: Choose how to represent a missing hand-added skill. It cannot run on the second device without its file.

options.label: Show missing
pros: The project still shows the choice you made and explains that the file needs to be added here.
cons: You may have to copy the file yourself to use that skill on this device.

options.label: Sync skill file
pros: A hand-added skill can work on another device without manually copying it.
cons: The skill's contents would travel between devices, unlike the marketplace install-only approach.

options.label: Local-only choice
pros: A device without the skill does not show an unusable entry.
cons: The project has different skill settings on different devices.
